Ardshinbank's own Armenian ArCa product page carries a dedicated section on the national scheme, separate from the tariff table: ' 2026 թվականի հունվարի 1-ից ՀՀ Ֆինանսների նախարարության և «Արմենիան Քարդ» ՓԲԸ-ի համատեղ ծրագրի շրջանակում Arca քարտերով իրականացված անկանխիկ վճարումների դիմաց ֆիզիկական անձանց տրամադրվում է cashback` վճարումների ընդհանուր գումարի 2%-ի չափով։' Caps match the national scheme exactly: 2% on domestic non-cash payments, minimum qualifying transaction 1,000 AMD, maximum 6,000 AMD per transaction, 60,000 AMD per month; excluded categories are utilities, government payments, high-risk merchants (gambling, adult, crypto), subscriptions, precious metals and financial-institution fees. The empty 'Cash-back' row the scan found belongs to Ardshinbank's own fee/tariff table (section 1, Հիմնական միջնորդավճարներ), i.e. the bank funds no cashback of its own — that is a different question from participation in the state/Armenian Card scheme, which sits outside the tariff table. Ardshinbank should be recorded as a participant alongside IDBank, Ameriabank, Conversebank, Evocabank and FastBank. Note the scheme is genuinely market-wide: Araratbank, Armeconombank, Unibank, ArmSwissBank, Acba and Inecobank all publish it too.

verification.question: Does any Armenian bank or fintech let a cardholder choose their own cashback categories each month (the T-Bank/Alfa/Plata mechanic)?
verification.verdict: CONFIRMED — no Armenian issuer offers customer-selected cashback categories
verification.detail: Searched in Armenian, Russian and English across the market, including the six scanned banks plus Acba, Inecobank, Unibank, AMIO, Araratbank, Armeconombank, ArmSwissBank, Evoca and the wallets Idram and Telcell, using the phrasings requested (ընտրովի կատեգորիաներ, выбранные категории кешбэк, категории кэшбэка на выбор, 'choose your cashback categories'). Every mechanic found falls into one of five fixed shapes, none of them customer-chosen: (1) flat rate on everything — Evocabank 0.25% on Visa Infinite/UnionPay Gold/Digital, Armeconombank ARMECs 1% uncapped, IDBank Visa Signature/Infinite 0.5%; (2) categories fixed by the issuer — IDBank Travel Card 1.5% abroad / 0.5% domestic, and the new Visa Wizz Air Platinum at 3% Wizz Air / 1.5% restaurants, supermarkets, accommodation and fashion / 1% everything else, all set by the bank; (3) [struck 2026-09-21 by A5: the "300 AMD/month fixed cash reward" on Acba cards does not exist — 300 AMD/month is the Visa Benefactor service fee via acba digital]; (4) merchant- or partner-specific promotions set by the issuer — Inecobank's 20% at Dalma Garden Mall, Idram/IDBank idcoin offers at 0.5–1.5%, Telcell wallet offers; (5) the national ArCa 2%, which is flat and state-defined. Two independent market-wide surveys by AFM (Armenian Financial Marketplace), read in both English and Russian, list the cashback mechanics of every significant Armenian issuer and contain no selectable-category product; the Russian edition states plainly that cashback is either credited on all transactions or tied to pre-defined categories, and the client cannot change the parameters himself. This is a negative finding across a market that could still add such a product without press coverage, so it is high-effort but not logically provable — confidence medium. The headline claim stands, and it remains a genuine white-space for FastBank.

verification.question: ArCa Pension 20% cashback (max 10,000 AMD, from 1 Jan 2026, replacing 12%/6,000): (a) who funds it; (b) is the cap per month or per transaction; (c) does it apply to pension cards at other Armenian banks?
verification.verdict: (a) It is state-funded: a Government of Armenia programme run by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs and paid from the state budget, not by Acba. (b) The 10,000 AMD cap is per month: 20% of the previous month's non-cash POS purchases, capped at 10,000 AMD, paid monthly. (c) Yes. Since 1 Jan 2024 it has applied to all pensioners and benefit recipients whatever their bank. Ararat Bank's ArCa pension card, for example, publishes the same terms.
verification.detail: (a) The programme began under Government decision N 723-Լ of 19.05.2022, with 10% cashback capped at 5,000 AMD per month. It was then a state-private partnership: the state paid 5% and partner banks 5%. Hetq (28.12.2023) reports that from 1 Jan 2024 the cashback 'վճարվում է բացառապես պետական բյուջեի միջոցների հաշվին՝ առանց բանկերի մասնակցության'. The Government meeting of 27.11.2025 (primeminister.am) raised the rate from 12% to 20% and the maximum from 6,000 to 10,000 AMD. The change runs to 31.12.2026 at a 2026 budget cost of about 14bn AMD, with Minister Arsen Torosyan presenting it. ARKA (25.06.2026) reports an extra 10bn AMD from the 2026 state budget. Acba's page does not name a funder for the 20%. It separately describes the 2% cashback for all ArCa cards as 'ՀՀ Ֆինանսների նախարարության և «Արմենիան Քարդ» ՓԲԸ-ի կողմից իրականացվող նախագիծ', and says ArCa Pension holders receive both (20% + 2%). (b) Acba's page states the cap without a period: '...կտրամադրվի 20% հետվճար, առավելագույնը 10,000 ՀՀ դրամ'. Ararat Bank's page gives the period: 'Տվյալ ամսում վճարման ենթակա հետվճարը հաշվարկվում է այդ ամսվան նախորդող ամսում կատարած անկանխիկ գնումների և վճարումների գործարքների 20 %-ի չափով, ոչ ավել 10,000 ՀՀ դրամ' and 'վճարվում է յուրաքանչյուր ամիս՝ մինչև տվյալ ամսվա 25-ը', credited to the pension bank account. How2B, iravaban.net, Civilnet and Sputnik Armenia all describe it as up to 10,000 AMD per month. (c) The same Hetq piece quotes the PM: from 1 Jan 2024 'բոլոր թոշակառուները և նպաստառուները' receive it, where it had earlier been limited to partner banks' clients. The underlying decision is N 723-Լ as amended. The 2025 amending decision's number was not found online, and welfare.gov.am pages did not render.

Entirely free to hold, AMD 0 minimum balance, free cash withdrawal at IDBank ATMs and only 0.50% at other Armenian banks - the cheapest cash access in the range. The product page publishes no cashback, but IDBank's ArCa Classic news item says pensioners with ArCa pension cards get the 2% campaign on top of an existing 20% cashback programme; this is not stated on the Caring card page itself, so it is recorded as unconfirmed for this product.
